metrics-meter-instrument-design.title: Design application metrics with Meter instruments
metrics-meter-instrument-design.short: Choose the measured quantity and tag cardinality deliberately
metrics-meter-instrument-design.summary: System.Diagnostics.Metrics provides standard counters, histograms, and other instruments for exposing application-specific measurements to observability systems.
metrics-meter-instrument-design.why: Ambiguous names or units and high-cardinality tags such as user IDs make aggregation harder and can greatly increase monitoring cost.
metrics-meter-instrument-design.tips: Use stable names and units, keep tag value sets bounded, and record measurements that drive decisions such as request counts, durations, and failures.

ibufferwriter-producer-pattern.title: Produce data through IBufferWriter<T> without intermediate copies
ibufferwriter-producer-pattern.short: Request writable space and advance only by bytes actually written
ibufferwriter-producer-pattern.summary: IBufferWriter<T> lets producers write directly into destination-provided Span or Memory without depending on one concrete array representation.
ibufferwriter-producer-pattern.why: Creating intermediate arrays for every chunk adds allocations and copies that can dominate high-throughput generation paths.
ibufferwriter-producer-pattern.tips: Never write past requested space, pass the actual written count to Advance, and do not retain returned memory across later buffer requests.

safefilehandle-ownership-lifetime.title: Make SafeFileHandle ownership and lifetime explicit
safefilehandle-ownership-lifetime.short: Represent operating-system file handles with managed lifetime rules
safefilehandle-ownership-lifetime.summary: SafeFileHandle safely owns file handles and can be passed to lower-level APIs such as RandomAccess while retaining managed lifetime semantics.
safefilehandle-ownership-lifetime.why: Keeping raw handle values around invites double-close and use-after-close bugs, especially when asynchronous I/O obscures how long the handle is needed.
safefilehandle-ownership-lifetime.tips: Choose one owner, keep the SafeHandle alive for every operation, and document whether callees borrow the handle or take ownership.

taskcompletionsource-inline-continuation.title: Keep TaskCompletionSource continuations out of the completion call
taskcompletionsource-inline-continuation.short: Completing a task can otherwise execute waiting code inline
taskcompletionsource-inline-continuation.summary: When adapting callbacks or events into Tasks, RunContinuationsAsynchronously separates waiting continuations from the thread that signals completion.
taskcompletionsource-inline-continuation.why: Calling SetResult while holding a lock can otherwise run arbitrary continuation work immediately, extending lock duration or reversing lock order.
taskcompletionsource-inline-continuation.tips: Consider this option for event bridges and use TrySet variants when completion, failure, and cancellation can race.

jsonserializeroptions-reuse-metadata-cac.title: Reuse JsonSerializerOptions instead of rebuilding serialization metadata
jsonserializeroptions-reuse-metadata-cac.short: Do not discard configuration and type metadata on every operation
jsonserializeroptions-reuse-metadata-cac.summary: JsonSerializerOptions participates in caching serialization metadata, so applications should normally share long-lived instances for each stable policy.
jsonserializeroptions-reuse-metadata-cac.why: Constructing equivalent options repeatedly on hot paths repeats setup and allocation work and prevents effective metadata reuse.
jsonserializeroptions-reuse-metadata-cac.tips: Keep a small set of reusable options, avoid mutating policy at runtime, and combine with source generation when startup or reflection cost matters.

aspnetcore-response-bodywriter-streaming.title: Stream ASP.NET Core responses through BodyWriter
aspnetcore-response-bodywriter-streaming.short: Avoid assembling a large response into one string or byte array
aspnetcore-response-bodywriter-streaming.summary: HttpResponse.BodyWriter exposes a PipeWriter so large responses can be generated progressively with fewer intermediate buffers.
aspnetcore-response-bodywriter-streaming.why: Building the whole response in memory increases peak usage, copying, and latency before the first bytes can be sent.
aspnetcore-response-bodywriter-streaming.tips: Flush at meaningful boundaries, observe RequestAborted, and benchmark the real pipeline including compression and middleware.

bounded-concurrency-queueing-vs-parallel.title: Design concurrency limits and queue limits separately
bounded-concurrency-queueing-vs-parallel.short: Limiting active work does not by itself bound waiting work
bounded-concurrency-queueing-vs-parallel.summary: A SemaphoreSlim can cap concurrent resource use, but overload remains if an unlimited number of callers are allowed to wait behind it.
bounded-concurrency-queueing-vs-parallel.why: When arrival rate exceeds capacity, unbounded waiting increases memory use and latency and makes recovery from incidents slower.
bounded-concurrency-queueing-vs-parallel.tips: Choose concurrency, queue capacity, timeout, and rejection policies together; use Channel or RateLimiter where they express the policy more directly.

string-create-allocation-aware-formattin.title: Format hot-path strings without unnecessary intermediate allocations
string-create-allocation-aware-formattin.short: Write the final representation without chains of temporary strings
string-create-allocation-aware-formattin.summary: string.Create-based formatting can write directly into the final string and avoid temporary concatenation objects in allocation-sensitive paths.
string-create-allocation-aware-formattin.why: Even small temporary strings accumulate GC cost when formatting runs at very high frequency.
string-create-allocation-aware-formattin.tips: Prefer ordinary interpolation for clarity first, then apply allocation-aware formatting only where profiling shows string creation is significant.

async-lock-held-across-io.title: Do not hold a lock across slow I/O
async-lock-held-across-io.short: Separate shared-state protection from unpredictable external work
async-lock-held-across-io.summary: Locks should protect short shared-state transitions while file, network, and other variable-latency operations happen outside the critical section.
async-lock-held-across-io.why: Holding a lock until I/O finishes stalls unrelated callers, and forcing async I/O into synchronous waits can compound the problem with ThreadPool starvation.
async-lock-held-across-io.tips: Capture the required snapshot under the lock, release it before await, and use versions or conflict checks if results must later be applied to changed state.

unity-job-dependency-lifetime.title: Align Unity Job dependencies with native-data lifetime
unity-job-dependency-lifetime.short: Native containers must outlive every job that uses them
unity-job-dependency-lifetime.summary: Unity Job System uses JobHandle dependencies to order work, and NativeArray or other native data must remain valid until all dependent jobs finish.
unity-job-dependency-lifetime.why: Dropping a dependency or disposing native storage too early can trigger safety errors or introduce data races.
unity-job-dependency-lifetime.tips: Combine dependencies from read/write relationships, avoid unnecessary early Complete calls, and dispose owned native data only after its final job use.
